description:
## Why this ticket exists

MCP is leg (2) of the product vision: a user's Claude answers "what did I spend this week per project". The v0.2 shape was set by Codex review: round 2 CUT `usage_hourly`, forced the cursor contract and the query-tz-equals-snapshot-tz rule; round 3 demoted the SDK choice to the T-009 release gate. Since then T-008 decided the coordination primitive and the SDK verdict plus consumption rules are recorded in N-003. **N-007/N-008 then CUT the reader computation lease entirely** — this text was repaired against that on 2026-08-04; see the repair log at the end.

## Scope — in

- **`spendbar mcp`** on the same bin; stdio transport; **stdout carries JSON-RPC only**, all logs to stderr (stdout purity is a T-009 conformance test).
- Tool layer sits behind the **~50-line adapter produced and validated by T-009** — never against an SDK directly. **SDK decided (T-009 verdict, N-003): adopt v2.** `@modelcontextprotocol/server@2.0.0` enters the ROOT manifest as a regular dependency pinned EXACT (no `^`/`~`) only when the production adapter lands in `src/mcp` — never while candidates live in the isolated spikes workspace; `zod` enters as an exact-pinned DIRECT dependency (T-009's phantom-dependency finding). Version bumps are deliberate acts gated by re-running T-009's conformance suite.
- **Exactly 5 tools**: `usage_summary`, `usage_by_project`, `usage_by_day`, `usage_share`, `usage_blocks`. **`usage_hourly` is NOT registered.** Do not register a stub.
- **Strict input schemas**: normalized start/end dates, provider filters, sort, limit, cursor; malformed input yields typed validation errors, never crashes (precedent: ISS-017).
- **v0.2 timezone rule**: the query timezone must equal the snapshot's IANA timezone — validation error otherwise; timestamp-level re-bucketing is future work.
- **Cursor contract**: a cursor encodes dataset generation id + normalized query + sort key + position; the referenced immutable generation is retained for a bounded period; expired cursors return a typed error requiring pagination restart; mismatched query/sort is rejected typed. Hard range/row caps; truncation + `nextCursor` metadata; summary-first defaults.
- **`outputSchema` registered once in `tools/list`**; every result = `structuredContent` + concise text fallback; `generatedAt`/freshness/coverage/warnings live INSIDE the registered result schema, derived per requested range/fields from T-010's per-dataset provenance — no global stale flag.
- **NO READER COMPUTATION — readers never compute** (N-007 decision 4). When the snapshot is stale, the answer is an **immediate honest-stale response** carrying freshness metadata. There is no lease, no lease port allocation, no `purpose` namespace, no wait deadline, no subprocess cap, no private temporary generation, and no herd contention — none of that machinery exists in this design. This closes ISS-079/ISS-080.
  - **SERVICE-STATUS SIGNAL — HELD on T-011 (ISS-086, reopened).** N-007 decision 4 also requires "an actionable service-not-running signal". That supplies AUTHORITY for the contract but not a WITNESS: no caller in this ticket can honestly know machine-wide service absence, and T-011 owns the only prospective coordination-state probe. Per L-006 the contract weakens to what is witnessable — a reader may report `undetermined` — and the true service-status portion is HELD on T-011's concrete probe. **Do not ship a signal that asserts "not running" on evidence this ticket can obtain.**
- **CLI gains `--cached`**: answer from the snapshot only, never invoking ccusage. `--cached` alters CLI surface the frozen oracle governs, so every user-visible divergence ships through the established parity mechanism — a numbered ALLOWLIST divergence entry plus replacement shipped-mode tests (ISS-026 pattern D); byte parity is untouched wherever the flag is absent.
- **CI measures tool-definition token cost — budget rule decided (N-003):** at completion, record the measured `tools/list` serialized size and proxy-token count for the 5 real tools as the committed baseline, and hard-gate CI at **baseline +10%**.

## Scope — out

- `usage_hourly`; timezone re-bucketing; MCP resources/prompts (tools only); any non-stdio transport.
- **Any reader-side computation, in any form** — cut by N-007 decision 4, and not to be reintroduced as an optimization.
- Registration UX: `claude mcp add`/`codex mcp add` consent prompts belong to the v0.3 setup wizard; `doctor`'s MCP-registration health checks and the real-client launch matrix are v0.3.

## Failure modes to test

- **Stale snapshot**: every reader returns an immediate honest-stale answer with freshness metadata. No waiting, no deadline, no computation. A mutant that adds a reader-side compute path MUST fail.
- **Concurrent refresh**: the writer publishes a new generation mid-pagination → the cursor stays pinned to its generation and pages remain mutually consistent until retention expires, then typed expiry.
- **Corrupt data**: quarantined generation ⇒ bounded partials from the known-good generation with warnings — no fabricated totals.
- **Protocol**: T-009's conformance suite (initialize, tools/list, tools/call, malformed input, cancellation, EOF, stdout purity) rerun over the final tool layer.

## Dependencies on gate outcomes

- **T-009 (hard — verdict recorded)**: SDK decision + adapter + real-client evidence; the tool layer is written against that adapter on the adopted v2 SDK.
- **T-010 (hard)**: all reads come from generation snapshots; freshness/coverage/warnings map from per-dataset provenance; cursor retention rides generation retention/GC; quarantine ⇒ bounded partials.
- **T-008 (COMPLETE — verdict consumed)**: with the lease cut, this ticket no longer instantiates the primitive at all; it is relevant only through T-011's service.
- **T-025 (HARD, via AC 4)**: `readGeneration(id)`. **Currently PARKED** (ISS-090/ISS-091).
- **T-011 (HARD, via AC 4 and via the service-status signal)**: the control-socket pin-request path, and the only prospective witness for service absence. **Currently PARKED**.
- **ISS-074 (HARD PREREQUISITE)**: this ticket's own constraints forbid npm lifecycle scripts, but the root `package.json` still declares **`prepack` and `prepare`**, and no shipping contract verifies the transitive lifecycle/native closure. **Even an adapter-only subset cannot merge honestly under this constraint**, and the packaging guarantees those two scripts currently supply must be replaced, not merely deleted.

## Constraints

No lifecycle scripts or native builds; `package.json` never carries an author field; no real transcript data or personal paths in fixtures; `usage.py` stays frozen. D5 byte-parity governs CLI text output (with `--cached` divergences riding the numbered ALLOWLIST), while **MCP structured outputs are separately versioned public schemas derived through adapters from the independently versioned internal snapshot schema** — NOT "internal schema written from MCP schemas".

## Exit

Week-per-project < 2 s warm from BOTH real clients (Claude Code and Codex).

## Acceptance criteria

1. `tools/list` returns exactly the 5 named tools, each with `outputSchema` registered once; a test asserts `usage_hourly` is absent.
2. Conformance suite green over the adopted v2 SDK behind T-009's adapter, **against recorded real-client transcripts**: initialize, tools/list, tools/call, malformed input (typed errors, no crash), cancellation, EOF; zero non-JSON-RPC bytes on stdout in any test.
   **THE TRANSCRIPT PORTION IS HELD pending ISS-088 and is NOT discharged by anything short of it.** T-009's real-client evidence is counters and SHA-256 digests plus a three-entry frame summary over a `spendbar_probe` tool (~4.4 KB) with **no replayable frame bodies** — so there is nothing to replay. A scripted conformance suite is independently landable **preparation** and explicitly does NOT discharge this AC. Only the owner may amend the requirement or authorize capturing replayable transcripts.
3. Timezone rule: a query whose timezone differs from the snapshot's IANA timezone returns a validation error naming both zones; an equal-timezone query succeeds.
4. Cursor contract: paging past the row cap yields truncation + nextCursor; all pages of one cursor are consistent with a single generation even when the writer publishes mid-pagination; after the referenced generation ages out of bounded retention, the cursor returns the typed expired error; a cursor whose embedded normalized query or sort key mismatches the request is rejected typed. **Consumes T-025's `readGeneration(id)` and T-011's pin-request path. BOTH ARE PARKED. This AC must not be attempted without them.**
5. Freshness honesty: with a stale snapshot, results carry freshness/coverage/warnings reflecting actual per-range coverage; with a quarantined generation, results are bounded partials from the known-good generation with warnings — never fabricated totals. **The service-status field reports `undetermined` unless T-011's probe is available; asserting "not running" without that witness is a defect, not a feature.**
6. **CUT** (N-007 decision 4). The reader computation lease and its herd test do not exist. Replaced by: with a stale snapshot, N ≥ 10 concurrent clients each receive an **immediate** honest-stale answer; no computation is started by any of them; a mutant introducing a reader-side compute path MUST fail.
7. `spendbar <view> --cached` spawns no ccusage subprocess (asserted via the injected runner) and returns snapshot-derived output with a freshness indication.
8. Parity: every user-visible divergence introduced by `--cached` has a numbered ALLOWLIST entry plus replacement shipped-mode tests, and the byte-parity suite stays green for all non-`--cached` invocations.
9. v0.2 phase exit: a week-per-project query completes in under 2 s warm from BOTH real clients.
10. Token budget (N-003): CI records the `tools/list` serialized size and proxy-token count; at completion these are committed as the baseline, and CI fails hard when either exceeds baseline +10%.

## Risks

Cursor-generation retention couples reader lifetimes to writer GC: a bug either leaks generations or breaks pagination mid-flight with untyped failures. The token-cost gate protects every user's context window at every client session start. **With the lease cut, the honest-stale path becomes the ONLY answer when the snapshot is stale** — so its wording is load-bearing UX, and the service-status field must not overclaim (see AC 5). SDK v2 surprises land here; the adapter plus T-009's v1 backend remain the contained fallback.

## Open questions (owner decisions)

1. Bounded retention period for cursor-referenced generations (the plan mandates 'bounded' but gives no number; it also sets T-010's GC floor of at least one known-good generation).
2. Scope of `--cached`: all 9 ported CLI views or only the snapshot-expressible subset? And its behavior when NO snapshot exists (typed error vs empty output).
3. Whether the v0.2 real-client exit test registers the server via the launcher's explicit `mcp` mode or via validated absolute paths.
4. **`usage_blocks` payload contract — ISS-089, unresolved and now sharper.** ISS-023/ISS-026 are resolved and name this ticket: "no validator lands in T-013". But every reader needs a payload schema and `blocks[]` is not uniform — a strict constructor IS runtime CCUSAGE_CMD validation. N-009's two-stage compat/normalize boundary was the obvious escape and was **rejected in T-025 review round 2**: stage 1 cannot turn a tolerated non-gap block with missing timestamps, `isActive: null` or absent `entries` into a strict row without inventing values, dropping a row the CLI displays, or making stage 2 refuse. The conflict stands with its escape closed.

*(Former open question 2 — reader-lease deadline and subprocess cap — is void: the lease is cut. Former question 4 on tool-token budget was decided in N-003.)*

**Related issues:** ISS-002, ISS-004, ISS-017, ISS-023, ISS-026, ISS-030, ISS-033, ISS-074, ISS-079, ISS-080, ISS-086, ISS-088, ISS-089

---

## Ticket-text repair log (2026-08-04)

Repaired BEFORE planning, per the standing rule that a re-plan's first act is fixing its own ticket text. **ISS-086** recorded that N-007 decision 4 CUT the reader computation lease while the ticket still carried its full design as live text. Sites 1–8 repaired in the first pass; sites 9–12 came from plan review and are repaired here.

1. **Scope bullet** — the ~200-word reader-lease paragraph (write-once `link()` allocation, `purpose` domain separation, no-takeover rule, bounded deadline, private temp generation, subprocess cap, herd load test) deleted, replaced with the honest-stale rule.
2. **Failure modes** — three rows deleted (no/crashed-service lease behaviour, herd, domain separation), replaced with one honest-stale row plus a mutant that MUST fail if reader-side compute reappears.
3. **AC 6** — was the herd test; now states the cut explicitly and asserts the replacement.
4. **Risks** — lease liveness hazards described machinery that no longer exists; replaced.
5. **Dependencies** — T-008's entry claimed this ticket instantiates the primitive as a lease namespace. It no longer instantiates it at all.
6. **Open question 2** (lease deadline + subprocess cap) was open for a cut feature. Voided; questions renumbered.
7. **Scope — out** now names reader-side computation explicitly.
8. **AC 5** gained the service-status field N-007 decision 4 requires.

From plan review round 1:

9. **THE TICKET TITLE** still read "5 bounded tools + **reader computation lease** + --cached" — the highest-visibility instruction in the filing, contradicting the repaired scope and N-007 #4. Renamed to "5 bounded snapshot tools + --cached". *(Eight body sites repaired and the title missed: the class-and-siblings pattern, again, in the very repair meant to fix it.)*
10. **AC 2 had been materially WEAKENED while I claimed it was only "recorded".** The transcript requirement was moved out of the operative sentence into a parenthetical, so a reader could discharge the shortened AC with no owner authorization. **Restored to the operative sentence and marked HELD**, with the scripted suite named as preparation that explicitly does not discharge it. Weakening an AC is an owner's act, not a planner's.
11. **The service-status signal had authority but no WITNESS.** Repeating N-007's requirement supplies authority; it does not name a caller that can honestly know machine-wide service absence — and T-011, which owns the only prospective probe, was listed as "otherwise not a blocker". Per L-006 the contract is weakened to a witnessable `undetermined` and the true status is HELD on T-011. **ISS-086 reopened** for this.
12. **ISS-074 added as a hard prerequisite.** This ticket forbids lifecycle scripts while the root manifest still declares `prepack` and `prepare`, with no contract verifying the transitive lifecycle/native closure — so even an adapter-only subset cannot merge honestly, and the packaging guarantees those scripts supply must be replaced rather than deleted.

park.reason:
PARK CONFIRMED BY THE REVIEWER, not self-certified. Verbatim: 'Park is correct; the three parks are causally connected, and no T-013 subset provides a coherent public surface while the five-tool payload contract remains blocked.' It answered my over-parking question directly: NOT over-parking, and none of the split candidates I considered (input schemas, timezone rule, --cached, token budget, honest-stale path) is worth shipping alone. All four review findings were defects I introduced in my own repair, and all four are now fixed.

THE CONTRADICTION, specifically — park criterion 3, a scope item that cannot be sound in isolation, and here the FILING SAYS SO ITSELF. AC 4 states verbatim: 'Consumes T-025's readGeneration(id) and T-011's pin-request path. BOTH ARE PARKED. This AC must not be attempted without them.' I parked both in this same session. The cursor contract is not peripheral — it is what makes every paged tool answer consistent. Compounding it: ISS-089 is unresolved and now HARDER, because N-009's two-stage compat/normalize boundary, the obvious escape from the CCUSAGE_CMD conflict, was rejected in T-025 review round 2 (stage 1 cannot turn a tolerated non-gap block with missing timestamps or null fields into a strict row without inventing values, dropping a row the CLI displays, or making stage 2 refuse).

WHAT N-009 DID FIX: ISS-087, last session's critical park reason — the payload fact grain is now decided as SnapshotPayloadV1. But T-025 implements it and is parked, so it exists as a decision and not as a type any reader can import.

DURABLE WORK THAT LANDED REGARDLESS: T-013's ticket text repaired at TWELVE sites. Eight in the first pass (the reader-lease design N-007 #4 cut was still live text throughout — scope bullet, three failure-mode rows, AC 6, risks, the T-008 dependency entry, open question 2, Scope-out, AC 5), and four more from review — including the TICKET TITLE, which still read 'reader computation lease' and is the highest-visibility instruction in the filing. Eight body sites repaired and the title missed is the class-and-siblings pattern inside the repair meant to fix it, and it is recorded as such.

TWO SELF-INFLICTED DEFECTS WORTH CARRYING FORWARD: I materially WEAKENED AC 2 while claiming I had only 'recorded' it (moved the transcript requirement out of the operative sentence into a parenthetical, so a reader could discharge the shortened AC without authorization) — restored and marked HELD. And I closed ISS-086 by citing N-007 #4's wording, which supplies AUTHORITY for the service-not-running signal but no WITNESS — no caller in T-013 can honestly know machine-wide service absence, and T-011 owns the only prospective probe while being listed as 'otherwise not a blocker'. ISS-086 REOPENED and narrowed to that question alone.

OWNER ACTIONS TO UNPARK, now five: (1) land T-025 items 2+5 — this single action also unblocks T-011's AC 1 and therefore the pin-request path; (2) rule on ISS-089; (3) amend AC 2 per ISS-088 or authorize capturing replayable transcripts; (4) settle ISS-074 WITH its replacement obligation — prepack/prepare's packaging guarantees must be replaced, not merely deleted, or even an adapter-only subset cannot merge honestly; (5) ratify ISS-086's witnessable 'undetermined' (recommendation (a), shippable immediately once ratified). Park record at docs/t013-park-n009.md.
